ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVdzeZs8AAAABcpxVMw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bpi2wzhGL8T0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bpi2w", "number": 17, "title": "Add interactive pose manipulation demo: drag/rotate limbs, full-body IK and MotionBricks responses (SOMA + MMD)", "body": "## Goal

Create a **separate interactive character manipulation demo** in `takahirox/three-motionbricks` where a person can grab a character's hand, foot, head, hip, etc. with the mouse, drag/rotate it, and see the **whole articulated body respond**, not merely move one disconnected bone. Combine that direct interaction with **MotionBricks-generated motion** so the character can react and transition naturally to user-directed poses.

Support the **native SOMA humanoid**, **MMD (Animasa Miku)** and **MMD (CG-CA Uka)** through a shared canonical SOMA rig and the existing MMD retargeting. **Do not replace or regress the current keyboard locomotion demo.**

### Intended experience

- On opening the new demo, show a stationary character in a suitable default/rest stance; no ONNX download or inference is required to start posing.
- Pick a visible joint/effector handle (e.g. left/right hand, foot, head, hips). **Drag to position** an end effector, or choose **rotate** to control joint orientation. For a hand drag, arm + shoulder + upper torso should follow as appropriate; for a foot drag, leg + hip/pelvis should respond, with configurable planted-foot support. Moving the pelvis/root translates the whole body coherently. Respect joint limits and avoid obviously impossible limb extension.
- The dragged target remains pinned under the cursor while dragging as closely as the rig permits. Release should not snap the character back to the original rest pose. Offer **Reset pose**, **Pause/resume generation**, model selector, and clearly marked `Move` / `Rotate` interaction modes.
- When the user opts into MotionBricks inference, the manipulated pose (and recent trajectory / target poses) becomes conditioning for **generated whole-body motion**; the user should see an intelligent response rather than a rigidly posed puppet. Keep held effector targets constrained via post-generation IK and smooth corrections where necessary.
- Clearly distinguish immediate IK updates from delayed *model-generated* motion. If WebGPU/ONNX is unavailable, manipulation should still work, with informative UI instead of pretending an IK-only response was generated by MotionBricks.

## Architecture and implementation

**1. New standalone page/entry point.** Add a separate demo URL (for example `/three-motionbricks/pose.html` or another documented route) with its own clean controls and build/Pages validation. Preserve the existing `index.html` locomotion behavior. Reuse renderer/avatar/MMD infrastructure rather than duplicating loading, allocation, cleanup or model asset logic.

**2. Shared canonical pose space.** Operate on `src/motion.ts`'s `Pose`, `Rig`, `JOINTS`, and world-space positions for the native SOMA skeleton. Map visible MMD effectors to corresponding canonical SOMA joints via existing `src/retarget.ts`; apply the result back to MMD through its existing retarget path. Handle model switching without stale selection/targets/physics resources. Do not assume MMD-specific extra bones appear in the 30-joint SOMA conditioning rig.

**3. Mouse controls + stable real-time IK.** Add visible pickable control points / gizmos and raycast/drag-plane positioning, with clear selected/hover feedback. Disable `OrbitControls` during active manipulation and restore camera control on release/cancel. Implement an appropriate constrained multi-joint IK / body-follow solver (e.g. weighted FABRIK/CCD/Jacobian or an existing suitable solution) for arms/legs and body/root, with configurable foot planting and sane reach/rotation limits. Work in consistent world/local transforms and avoid one-frame lag, invalid quaternions, jumps or bone detachment. Rotation mode should work on useful joints; position mode should move affected parent-chain/body in a predictable way, not only the selected bone's local translation.

**4. MotionBricks conditioning rather than fabricated playback.** The existing `src/motion.ts` `encode(context, targets, rig)` consumes **four recent full-body context poses plus four full-body target poses**. Existing `targetsFor()` authors walk/run stride goals; do not assume the ONNX model directly accepts a mouse coordinate, a partial hand constraint, or a guaranteed hard IK target. Derive feasible full-body conditioning poses/trajectories from the IK solution, supply them via the existing seven SOMA feature tensors and inference worker, and experiment with target trajectories/strength and stable transitions. Maintain a truthful distinction between an observed response and a guaranteed trained capability; if unconstrained model generations miss the dragged effector, apply a bounded post-generation IK correction without erasing the rest of the generated motion. Avoid repeatedly restarting inference on every pointer-move: throttle/coalesce intents, invalidate stale generations, smoothly hand off from immediate pose to generated sequence, and handle delayed results/underruns.

**5. MMD secondary simulation.** Preserve Animasa/Uka Toon/outline and physics. Apply motion/IK before physics as appropriate, keep grabbed/controlled joints authoritative, prevent the physics solver from fighting actively manipulated limbs, and allow hair/skirt/etc. to respond naturally. Ensure SOMA and MMD geometry/rig resources are disposed properly.

**6. Separate concerns and scope.** Create testable modules for pointer-to-effector targeting, IK solver, pose target/conditioning generation and playback/transition. Reuse `src/player.ts`, `src/inference.ts` and existing worker where possible. Do not alter/download/relicense model assets, change ONNX weights, or break keyboard locomotion. No retraining is required for an initial feasibility implementation.

## Suggested implementation stages (within this Issue)

1. **Manipulation MVP:** independent page; SOMA and both MMD avatars can be selected, stationary poses displayed, drag-and-rotate handles work with connected-chain IK, root/body follow and planted-feet options. Works **without** ONNX.
2. **MotionBricks integration:** button to load model, four-frame IK-conditioned targets/context, generated response, blending, active effector constraints, generation status and robust cancellation. Include at least hand-reach and foot-move examples.
3. **Polish + verification:** physics interactions, model switching/reset/camera, UI/UX, resource cleanup and the full existing-demo regression suite. Document demonstrated successes and model limitations instead of claiming arbitrary-pose compliance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New GitHub Pages-accessible interactive-pose demo exists, with a link from README/current demo; original locomotion demo still works.
- [ ] SOMA, Animasa Miku and Uka can be selected and manipulated in the same interface; first pose interaction works without starting/download of MotionBricks.
- [ ] Dragging a **hand** moves linked arm/shoulder/torso; dragging a **foot** affects leg/pelvis and handles grounded support; dragging **hips/root** coherently moves the body. Rotation mode and Reset work.
- [ ] Joint limits, reach constraints, foot-contact policy and mouse/camera pointer ownership are predictable; no unbounded stretch, broken skinning or NaN transforms.
- [ ] When ONNX is loaded, manipulate at least one hand/foot and observe an **actual MotionBricks-generated full-body sequence**, blended from the current pose, distinct from pure IK. Document target conditioning and evidence (diagnostic counters / motion trace and captures); don't claim all poses are controllable without testing.
- [ ] Held effectors remain appropriately constrained through generation (bounded post-IK as needed); changes mid-inference and model switching cannot apply stale results.
- [ ] Missing WebGPU, model download failure, and unsupported/poor model responses degrade gracefully to useful IK-only manipulation and an honest status.
- [ ] MMD toon/outline and secondary physics work with the interaction; no fights over controlled joints, leaking allocations, or regressions when switching SOMA/MMD.
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover IK convergence/limits, conditioning shape & finiteness, target transitions/cancellation and mappings; available browser smoke tests cover drag handles, rotation, page navigation and reset. Existing tests/build/`check:pages`/Pages deployment succeed.
- [ ] README and brief user-facing instructions describe controls, inference needs, and known limitations.

Relevant existing code: [`src/motion.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/src/motion.ts), [`src/player.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/src/player.ts), [`src/avatar.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/src/avatar.ts), [`src/mmd.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/src/mmd.ts), [`src/retarget.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/src/retarget.ts).

**Priority:** user-facing new demo.
